DEC-081 (2026-09-27, operator "approve D62 as written") — THE PRICE PAGE. (A) Negotiable is a toggle beside the amount, stored as `listings.price_negotiable`, with a "Negotiable" badge beside the price on the card, the detail and the admin table and a feed filter; `negotiable` stops being a price mode. (B) The leaf's pricing-basis attribute ("per hour / per job / fixed / quote") is asked on the price step, above the amount, not on Specifications; the doors judge it at step 5; D44 locks and prefills are unchanged; Review shows it under Price. (C) Currency: the default chain is saved → last listing → the seller's home country's currency → IP country → ETB; the list opens with that currency first, USD second, then a curated commonness order; every row shows code, symbol and name; `currencies` gains `symbol` and `display_order`, so opening Kenya, Somalia, Djibouti or Eritrea costs one row each in `countries.currency_code`. Rationale: the operator's ruling that the price page is where a seller naturally says the price is negotiable, that the currency of the country the seller posts from must come first with the most common currency (usually USD) next, and that symbols help recognition. This is ruling D62 of the previous block; DEC-081 had been reserved for it. Status (2026-10-04): built and landed in the five turns above (`6ebe04ea`, `0bbf9eb7`, `394162bb`, `9690a9d3`, `1f7e0869`; marks `20260928040000`, `20260928060000`, `20260928090000` on prod and staging). Deferred piece: the feed's "negotiable only" filter chip waits for the feed-filters spec (no filter surface exists yet). Later amendments recorded elsewhere: on 2026-09-30 part (B) was amended for goods (a `unit_of_sale-` basis is asked on the specifications step; service bases stay on the price step) — an amendment itself reversed by DEC-109 (2026-10-02): the unit of sale is asked on the price page again (N2 retired, DEC-121) — and bundle 4 (2026-10-04) moved the price page ahead of the title page (decided 2026-10-02 as DEC-110 "TITLE AND DESCRIPTION COME AFTER THE PRICE", block S50; the door's step numbers follow as DEC-120, block S51; screens A + B landed 2026-10-04, `roadmap.md` "Screens A + B — done (steps 1–11; PW-135, PW-136–139 …)").

CATEGORY IMAGES — INC-308 AND DEC-082. The executor's read-only investigation could not capture the failing call (it cannot sign in as an admin: the Supabase project is external to it) but established that the route's own refusals are JSON and that the pipeline burns 130–180 ms of CPU per image on the Worker. The supervisor froze the decision rule before the operator's capture: "if the body is a Cloudflare error page (or anything non-JSON), DEC-082 = option (a)". The capture showed the hosting platform's HTML error page, and the rule decided. The build turn landed as `0bf75959` (Tier B, no migration, no policy change; its own run 36382822067 was cancelled by the next push, and the first green board carrying it is `9690a9d3`): the route keeps the gate, the body checks, the category read, the prompt and the provider call and returns `{ stage: "generated", prompt, genMs, image: <base64> }` with `Cache-Control: no-store`; new `src/features/admin-categories/category-image-variants.ts` cuts the card (512), thumb (128) and OG (1200×630) variants on canvas with the old pipeline's constants; the service uploads `card-<ts>.png`, `thumb-<ts>.png` and `og-<ts>.png` under `<categoryId>/` to the bucket `category-assets` under the admin's session and `admin_set_category_images` saves the links; failures carry a stage (model-call, process, upload, persist, client-timeout); `pipeline.ts`, `raster.ts`, `raster.test.ts` and `font.ts` are deleted and declared in `docs/tracking/intentional-deletions.txt`; tests CI-1, CI-2, CI-2b, CI-4b, CI-4 rewritten to the new contract. pngjs, jpeg-js and @types/pngjs stay in `package.json` because `scripts/fixtures/photos/make.ts` imports them. Executor limitations recorded: its sandbox holds a real Gemini key and the first local test run spent a few image credits; the real provider sends JPEG, not PNG (CI-2's PNG check holds only in fake mode). Operator acceptance walk 2026-09-28: "11 generated · 0 failed".

DEC-082 (2026-09-27, decided by a rule frozen before the evidence) — CATEGORY IMAGE VARIANTS ARE CUT IN THE ADMIN'S BROWSER; THE WORKER ONLY CALLS THE PROVIDER. The generate route calls the image provider and returns the generated image; the admin console cuts the card, thumb and OG variants in the browser and uploads them under the admin's own session; the existing door `admin_set_category_images` saves the links. No migration and no storage-policy change were needed: holders of `categories:assets` could already write to `category-assets` (policies in `20260903114705`, public read in `20260903105611`). Rationale: bulk "Generate image" died in the hosting layer with an HTML 500 (INC-308); whether the Worker ran out of CPU decoding the image or failed loading the image libraries, the cure is the same — no image processing and no image library on the Worker. Rejected: the two other options examined — (b) a Supabase Edge Function doing the processing, (c) a provider-side resize. Status (2026-10-04): built and landed (`0bf75959`; green board at `9690a9d3`, run 36388786851); accepted by the operator's walk of 2026-09-28. Leftovers closed in W1: INC-310 and the stale sentence in `docs/features/categories.md`.

INC-317, THE PW-61 FLAKE — ROOT CAUSE IN THE APP, FIXED IN THREE TAKES. The investigation turn (`c34b727b`, changelog line only) found a real-seller bug: a late currency prefill queued a step no longer on screen. Take 1 (queue reads the step on screen, plus dropping a currency answer that arrives after the price step closed) failed its own repeat run — PW-72 as written 24 of 24 (a test fault) and PW-61 "Undo within ten seconds" 19 of 24 (real: the dropped write was what mirrored the door's own currency fill) — and the executor's "undo" restored the already-committed version (`7a020e55`), so `dev` carried the failed attempt. Take 2 (`18f1b592`, run 36414969833 red) restored `step-pricing.tsx` and kept only `stepRef`; PW-72's second assertion was wrong (a step-4 autosave on photos is legitimate once details was finished). Its run 36435962253 was red in the Build job (INC-326) and exposed a blind spot: CI uploaded browser-test logs only when a job failed, so on a green run both new sections read "No … lines (or no log was uploaded)" — the check was blind and read as clean (the executor's report had named the smoke-log half of this as a limitation). R1 ("the red and the blind census"; `4e2a9aad`, run 36494534782, green at 2026-09-28 23:09 UTC, promoted) fixed both: the `.prettierignore` entry; the smoke, shard and email log-capture steps run `if: always()`; the a11y tests are tagged `@a11y` and the shards run `--grep-invert "@global-state|@a11y"`, so the pass runs once, in the smoke tier; each section opens with "Logs read: <sources> · unavailable: <sources or none>" and never states zero for a log it could not read. The only red job in that run was the fast lane, which is signal-only; its report showed no failure behind the red (watch: a second unexplained fast-lane red gets an incident). The first real census read "Logs read: all 9 · unavailable: none" and listed six messages off the allowlist: "listing not found" ×102 (INC-323), the card-rank duplicate key (INC-327) and four deliberate refusals later attributed to their tests in W2. DEC-083 (2026-09-28, operator "please proceed with your proposal") — SERVER-ERROR CENSUS ON EVERY RUN. Text as recorded in `docs/features/e2e-harness.md`: "DEC-083 — Server-error census (2026-09-28). Every run, green or red, writes a "Server errors — census" section: [ssr-error] lines from every source, counted by normalised message. Messages on docs/tracking/ssr-error-allowlist.txt are counted but quiet; an allowlist entry must name the test that provokes it, and a message no test can be shown to provoke stays off the list. Gating rule, pre-committed: the census is non-gating for 14 days from 2026-09-28. During that window any SQL-class line on a green run (SQLSTATE classes 22, 23 or 42 — messages containing "violates", "does not exist" or "null value") receives an INC the same day. From 2026-10-12, once five consecutive runs have carried zero off-allowlist SQL-class lines, the merged verdict fails on any new off-allowlist SQL-class line; a message added to the allowlist after that date needs a DEC." Rationale: the failure reporter quoted `[ssr-error]` lines only for a failed source (capped at 20), so a swallowed exception on a green run was invisible. The number DEC-083 had first been reserved, earlier the same day, for the D66 publish attestation "when its prompt ships"; that reservation lapsed when the number was used here, and D66 never received a DEC number in this period. Status (2026-10-04): built and live, non-gating (`694689f6`, corrected by R1 `4e2a9aad`); gating becomes possible from 2026-10-12, once five consecutive runs have carried zero off-allowlist SQL-class lines.

DEC-085 (2026-09-29, supervisor decision on the operator's known-product directive) — ONE RULE FOR EVERY FIELD TYPE: SETTLED MEANS FILLED AND HIDDEN. A detail the chosen product fixes to one value is filled and hidden, whether it is a pick-list, a number, a year or a yes/no; the review page and the preview still show it and the door still judges it. A fact that is only the most common variant (a storage default, for example) stays editable (operator ruling of 2026-09-20). Yes/no facts need a small addition to the catalogue format so the curator can lock them. Rationale: the operator's earlier rulings (D44 of 2026-09-22, and 2026-09-27) had reached only one kind of field, a pick-list narrowed to exactly one answer. Measured by the supervisor on its copy of the catalogue: 240 numbers fixed to one value were filled but shown editable (iPhone 13 battery, 3,227 mAh), 246 years fixed to one value were not even filled (release year 2021), and 307 yes/no facts could not be locked (306 of them "dual SIM"). Status (2026-10-04): built for numbers and years in W4 (`4de0e33f`; `pinnedNumber`; test PW-76); the yes/no lock, and the same fill-and-hide for a link scope that leaves one value, were assigned to a turn named W4b that was never issued — `docs/features/posting.md` still reads "Yes/no pins are deferred to W4b" at dev `48d3c53b` (line 1079); W4b was never issued and is named in no later source (blocks S46–S53).

DEC-086 (2026-09-29, operator "big YES") — THE EXACT-MODEL QUESTION IS REQUIRED. An exact-model question is required whenever the chosen series or make offers more than one model. The seller can still pick "Other" when the model is not listed; then no specs fill in and the seller answers them. The database enforces it when a draft is saved, not only the form. The rule is defined by behaviour, not by name: a dependent pick-list (a definition with `depends_on`) whose options carry `facts`, `allowed` or `bounds` for other details is required once its parent is answered and the parent's chosen value offers more than one child option; the two card questions stay mandatory as before. Rationale: a known product's fixed specs sit on the model question, which was optional, so a seller who skipped it was asked everything; a seller always knows the exact model, and that one answer removes several questions. Status (2026-10-04): built and landed. Door: `validate_listing_draft` re-declared whole from its base `702a2975` in `20260929093107_1dc182d8` → mark `20260929180000` on prod and staging (`58bfd6d7`, run 36549793568; 51 lines added, none removed; proofs P19–P21); at step 3 and later an empty such list is refused `{attr_key, reason: 'required'}`; as landed the list must also be visible, and the count is of active, allowed child options ("Other" counts). Form mirror (`requiredByModel`: required mark and soft border from the moment the rule applies) and route test PR-16 in `4de0e33f`; big lists covered by INC-336 in W5. Accepted consequence: the series level is also required where a brand has several series with fixed specs (Apple → iPhone 13).

DEC-087 (2026-09-29, operator "tests are taking longer than 20 mins and as said before we need to improve that") — CI TIMING CENSUS AND THE SPLIT JUDGE. Every CI report carries a non-gating timing section, and the two largest spec files are split by area without changing any test. Judge, frozen before any number existed: "the split is kept as a win if the median push→report wall time over the next three green CI runs is ≤ 19 minutes (80 % of the current ~24-minute median); if not, the timing section names the new long pole and nothing else changes without a new DEC." Rule recorded with it: the spec file is the shard unit, so no spec file carries more than about 25 tests per project; a file that would grow past that is split first. Rationale: `playwright.config.ts` sets `fullyParallel: false`, so a spec file is never split between shards and one large file is one shard's long pole; `post-wizard.spec.ts` (76 tests) and `admin-attributes.spec.ts` (64) were the two largest. Other levers (a bigger staging database, skipping browser tests on docs-only commits) wait until the timing section shows they are needed. Status (2026-10-04): built and landed (CI-T1, `7c300b6e`); the judge was MET on 2026-09-29 — the three green runs after the split took 14.3, 18.7 and 14.1 minutes from push to report (median 14.3); the slowest shard fell from about 20 minutes to 12.4.

THE PLACE STEP — W6, W6-R AND THE W6b DESIGN.
- Spec and approval. On the W4 walk the operator passed the place step with only the country chosen and ruled: "I THINK WE SHOULD FORCE SELECTION UP TO A CITY JUST LIKE WHAT WE DID WITH CATEGORY AND SHOULD BE RED IF NOT SELECTED … SUBCITY IS OPTIONAL", with additional places laid out as in the reference project apex. The supervisor's W6 spec was approved the same day ("AGREE W6"). Operator rulings carried by the prompt: R1 the item's location must be a city, a sub-city is optional, and the place heading and box wear the required mark and soft border until a city is chosen; R2 every place the listing is shown in is a city or a sub-city, and a region or a country alone never counts; R3 the prefill stays; R4 nested layout — a country box contains region boxes, a region box contains its cities, with the add buttons inside the box they extend; R5 the plan decides which add buttons appear (free plan: 1 city, 1 region, 1 country, so none).
- DEC-064 AMENDED (2026-09-29, operator "AGREE W6"). DEC-064 had allowed coverage at any level. Now every coverage place is a city or a sub-city; the door's `multipleMarkets` refusal is retired and countries are counted against the plan's `max_countries`; "everywhere" stays a later paid option.
- The executor's stop and the rulings on it. The executor stopped at the prompt's own stop rule with three findings, all confirmed by the supervisor's read: `submit_listing` calls `validate_listing_draft` with the step being saved, so places sent below step 6 were stored unjudged; the step-6 query wrote `v_lands` twice, so the country limit counted country-level places instead of countries; and the place step had never prefilled from the last listing. Rulings: (1) places are judged whenever they are sent, at any step, in the one door — never silently ignored, because dropping input silently is phantom success — while "coverage required" stays at step 6 and later (proof P27); (2) `v_lands` fixed in the same re-declaration, with a class scan for the same double write; (3) the last-listing prefill is not part of W6 (R3 corrected to "the existing prefill (saved-area cookie → location guess) stays"; S72). A read-only live count found 10 listings with a region-level place (6 drafts, 4 in screening, none published); no data was rewritten.
- W6 first landing (`0e4adb22`; migration `20260929201601_a3a572bf` → mark `20260929235900`, applied on prod): the door rule `cityRequired`, the nested layout, plan limits from the schema (`PLAN_CITIES` deleted), six new strings in English and Amharic ("Choose a city." and the layout labels); tests PR-17, PW-80, PW-81, PW-82 and a component test. The migration then failed on staging (INC-340) and CI was red (run 36626287215).
- W6-R, the repair — LANDED CLEAN (`d662a91f`; migration `20260929205914_13cb1b22` → marks `20260930001000` and `20260929235900`; Tier B plus migration). Proofs build their own scratch markets (INC-340); the door counts distinct cities, regions and countries (INC-341; proofs P22–P29); the description limit follows the door's 5,000 (INC-342; PR-18); PR-17 seeds its own scratch region, city and sub-city. The executor's first apply attempt failed on a JSON syntax error in its own code for picking free country codes; nothing was applied. On staging the operator applied only `13cb1b22`; `a3a572bf` is recorded there by mark only and must never be applied there. The executor's local DEC-023 suite on staging: 207 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed, none flaky (17.9 minutes). Run 36630568746 was red before the staging apply and green on re-run; promoted. The operator's walk steps 1–6 passed and W6 was closed on 2026-09-29. Left for W6b: INC-343 and one unused translation string ("All the places must be in one market").
- The W6b design (operator, 2026-09-29). The country/region/city list is where the advertisement is shown; beside each listed place a choose-one marker says this is where the advertised item or service is (exactly one, a city or a sub-city); the map centres on that place with an optional exact pin; the pin is the item's spot, and a tick "this is also my shop/office" saves it to the seller's profile. The operator asked to be questioned for clarification; four multiple-choice questions were put, and the recorded answers are: the map only where it matters (it stays a category setting); the pin is the item or service spot and a tick saves the shop/office (also editable in Settings); the next post prefills the last post's places and marked item place, without the pin, with a one-tap "Use my shop location"; the saved shop/office is shown on the seller card and storefront, not on every post. Decided with it: the work is Tier A (a shop location on the profile is personal data: owner-only read and edit, included in export and deletion, rounded to about 500 m on public pages unless the seller chose "exact"); showing the shop/office to buyers becomes a requirement of the listing-page and storefront builds, which do not exist yet.
- After the W6 walk the operator asked for a separate city box under each region, "Add region" inside the country box and "Add city" inside the region box as the admin plan allows, a tick beside each city for the item location, and a map that opens centred on that place where a pin can be dropped and saved ("I opened the map and no opetion to drop a pin and save and appears slow … please understand apex very well for this"). The supervisor had the reference repo studied read-only (apex uses Leaflet with Mapbox map images fetched with a key from a small server function and OpenStreetMap as fallback; it draws the chosen city's outline, lets the seller tap to drop a draggable pin, search an address or use "my location", and confirm) and split W6b in three: W6b-1 the layout, the single "Item or service is here" tick and the prefill from the last post (Tier B, no door change, no migration; prompt issued 2026-09-29 on base `d662a91f`, with tests PW-83 and PW-84 in a new `e2e/post-wizard-where.spec.ts`); W6b-2 the map rebuilt the apex way; W6b-3 the shop/office location on the profile. W6b-1's rulings: the step is where the ad is shown (heading "Where should this ad be shown?"); a city box appears only after its region is chosen and stays at least 280 px wide at 360 px; exactly one tick, sent first in the coverage list because the door's item place is `p_coverage[1]`; any city box can be removed while another remains, and removing the ticked one moves the tick; prefill order for a new post — the seller's most recent other listing (read with an explicit `seller_id` filter), then the saved-area cookie, then the location guess. The map-service choice for W6b-2 (Mapbox as in apex, or the free OpenStreetMap servers) was put to the operator, who asked first what is best for performance and budget at scale and whether a fast free alternative exists; the answer and everything after it belong to the next block.

DEC-089 (2026-09-29, PROPOSAL ONLY; operator "wE WILL DISCUSS THOSE LATER") — A COUNTRY-LOCALISED CATALOGUE THROUGH TWO ADDITIVE DATA LAYERS. Proposed, not decided: (1) per choice, "offered only in these countries" (an untagged choice is offered everywhere, so today's catalogue needs no change); (2) per question, "ask only in these countries" and "prefill differently by country". Principles: the country the item is posted in decides what is offered, not the seller's nationality; old listings never break; "Other" stays everywhere and typed answers are collected per country; there is always one list per question, never a copy per country; a tag means "markets where this is sold", because an Ethiopian mart abroad sells Ethiopian products. Already per country in the repo: every listing records its country; each country has its currency, unit system and order of top-level categories; a category can be hidden in chosen countries. To carry into the decision when it is taken: the ETB fallback at `pricing-data.ts:196` and the 11 fields whose help text names Ethiopia. Proposed build trigger: before the first market outside the Ethiopian and Eritrean community opens (Kenya or Somalia), or sooner if a walk finds a wrong default in a diaspora country. ESTIMATE: 4–7 executor prompts for both layers with tests, more if browse filters also need country scoping. Status (2026-10-04): proposal, parked by the operator; no later record under this number.

MAP PROVIDER (decided 2026-09-30). The supervisor's first comparison (2026-09-29) recommended staying on free OpenStreetMap and moving to map data self-hosted on the operator's Cloudflare account (Protomaps, about $5–12 a month) before launch. The operator asked for a re-analysis on "best uer experience, lightweight and easy to use, secure not expensive"; the second pass added satellite view (sellers in Ethiopia find a place by landmarks, not street names) and Esri's free tier, and recommended Esri: ArcGIS Location Platform Static Basemap Tiles, streets and imagery, on the existing Leaflet library; free allowance as read from the pricing page 2,000,000 tiles a month, then $0.15 per 1,000 (ESTIMATE: 20–40 tiles per map session, so about 50,000–100,000 seller map sessions a month). Compared and not chosen: Mapbox, which the operator's apex app uses (street 200,000 free loads a month then $0.50 per 1,000; satellite 750,000 free then $0.25 per 1,000); MapTiler and Stadia (free plans do not allow business use); OpenFreeMap and Protomaps (no satellite, a heavier map library). Operator, 2026-09-30: "agree with your recomendation for asri, but we still need to have a backup built so if one doenst work we still have a fall baclk and a way to see on admin side if one is working and tracking cost". Built in W6b-2 with OpenStreetMap as the automatic fallback; self-hosting is reconsidered only if use passes about 1.5 million tiles a month for two months in a row. The apex app (`tesfayekb/apex-marketplace`, `src/components/maps/MapPinDropper.tsx`) is the reference for the pin experience only, not for its browser-side Nominatim calls or its token handling. Buyers do not load live maps by default (a map picture made once, or a "Show map" tap). The earlier promise to put "Cloudflare-hosted maps before launch" on the launch checklist lapsed with this decision; `docs/governance/launch-gate.md` carries no map line. Not confirmed: business use on Esri's free tier (the operator was asked to check the terms at sign-up).

DEC-091 (2026-09-30, operator "approve both above") — ADMIN › SERVICES: EVERY OUTSIDE SERVICE IS TRACKED FOR HEALTH AND COST. One admin page with a row per outside service: a status light and last check; the error rate over the last 24 hours; usage this month against the free allowance; estimated cost against a budget the operator sets; which backup is in use. Services found in code: Supabase, Google Gemini (AI images, writing help), Google Translate, Nominatim (address lookup), OpenStreetMap, Esri, Telegram (sign-in); outside the code: Cloudflare, Lovable hosting, GitHub Actions, the email sender (the build confirms the full list). Health: a scheduled check every 15 minutes plus a success/failure count of every real server call. Usage and cost: exact for calls the server makes; estimated for map images, which phones fetch directly (Esri's own usage page stays the truth); hosting bills read from usage APIs where they exist, otherwise entered monthly; prices editable in admin. Alerts: an email to admins when a service is down, passes 80 % of its free allowance, or passes its budget. Backups: maps switch automatically (Esri → OpenStreetMap); the existing per-AI-feature on/off control moves to this page. Security: keys stay on the server; a services permission gates the page. Scope added the same day: API-key expiry dates, so admin warns before the Esri key runs out. Rationale: the operator's standing directive of 2026-09-30, "everyoutside resource we have /we use need to be tracked, like clusdeflare, supabase, the ai with all the costs and if those are working(a way to detect and need to have that interface inside admin". Status (2026-10-05): approved, not built — queued on 2026-09-30 after the flaky-test turn (CI-T2); no prompt was ever issued and no later mention exists through turn 1375 or in block S53; the map route's fallback log line (`src/routes/api/map/tiles.ts:113`) is written for it to count. The Esri API key created 2026-09-30 expires at most one year after creation; nothing warns before it does until this page exists.

DEC-093 (2026-09-30, supervisor, flagged to the operator, who did not comment) — A VARIANT-SPLIT CELL COUNTS AS SETTLED FOR CATALOGUE COVERAGE. The curator works to a pre-committed bar: at least 95 % of a leaf's fact cells settled before its files ship (§8.3 of its rules). Buses & Vans stood at 94.9 % (74 of 78). The ruling, as sent to the curator: "a cell proven variant-split by two independent market sources, with no dominant variant, counts as settled for §8.3 coverage. Buses & Vans passes." Rationale: the Karry K60 is sold in Ethiopia with both gearboxes (Jiji: two manual 2022 petrol, one automatic 2025 electric; Cari: four automatics, one manual; the maker sells both), so no research can close the three open cells, and holding the leaf would block useful fixes (the coach seat locks, removing Offer Type). "K60 EV" is added as a model only when a battery and range source exists. Rejected: holding the leaf until fleet evidence shows a dominant version. Status (2026-10-04): in force; reused the same day for motorcycles (Boxer, HLX and Star as two-choice lists) and as the two-source bar for locking Yadea and Dodai to Electric (INC-358).

DEC-094 (2026-09-30, supervisor ruling on the operator's directive "are we going to make that message localized to ethiopia? … please put in knopwledge base") — MARKET-NEUTRAL WORDING AND THE `{country}` TOKEN. No UI string and no catalogue text (labels, options, helps) names Ethiopia or any one country where the statement depends on the seller's or buyer's market; such text is written with a `{country}` token that shows the market's country name in the screen's language. Product and cultural facts (teff, the Ethiopian calendar, a brand's name, cuisine) are not market statements and stay. Rationale: the Clothing walk showed the help "Sellers in Ethiopia choose Ethiopian-made." and the Amharic answer «እዚሁ የተሰራ» duplicating «የኢትዮጵያ ምርት»; texts tied to one country are hard to find and rewrite when a second market opens. Engine (executor Part T3): one resolver; the market comes from the draft's or listing's market, then the seller's detected market, then the fallback en "the seller's country" / am «የሻጩ ሀገር»; admin and exports show the raw token; the import gate accepts `{country}` and refuses any other `{…}` token; the finder indexes token-bearing text with the token removed. Line for `AGENTS.md` (Part T2), verbatim: "MARKET-NEUTRAL WORDING (DEC-094): UI strings and catalogue text (labels, options, helps) never name Ethiopia or any one country where the statement depends on the seller's or buyer's market; write it with the {country} token. Product and cultural facts (teff, the Ethiopian calendar, a brand's name) are not market statements." Curator rule from the same day: write no new market-specific text; convert existing rows only when told the token has landed. Rulings on the curator's census (`c27-dec094-market-wording-census-2026-09-30.csv`: 10 rows name the market, 4 are Ethiopia-only systems): (1) six neutral rewrites that need no token (voltage, `shoe_size_system`, `kibe_origin`, `net_weight_g`, honey "Yemen", `brand-salon` "Workshop-made (local)") done at once, in the Construction batch; (2) "Made in": `product_origin` survives and `origin-food` merges into it, with two answers, "Made in {country}" / «የ{country} ምርት» (value `local_made`) and "Imported"; this and the other token rows (`condition-vehicles` "Used in Ethiopia", `imei_registered`) wait for the token; (3) "Class B", Ethiopia-only systems that name no country (`plate_code`, `title_status`, `condo_scheme`, "libre" in the engine help), deferred until a second market opens, when a question will need to be shown only in certain countries. Later additions: country-dependent presets (220 V, EU shoe sizes, Wi-Fi-only tablets, electric cookers, locally made, rebar 12 m) and per-market units (lb, US gallons, cu ft, inches) wait for the same mechanism as per-market defaults. Status (2026-10-05): decided and BUILT in bundle 4 — door half in M6 `20261004212627_e44f20e5` (mark `20261005100000`, on ethio-prod and ethio-staging; `attr_cell_check` accepts `{country}` anywhere and refuses any other brace token except a valid `{category:<slug>}` in help text; `/api/translate` masks every brace token); screens in turn 9b, `0fc968e4` (2026-10-05 00:58Z): `src/i18n/catalog-tokens.ts` (catalogPieces / drawCatalog / catalogWords, `TOKEN_RE`), `src/features/posting/catalog-scope.ts` + `catalog-scope-provider.tsx` (tokenCountryCode: the ad's first place → the area cookie → the CONFIRMED home country → null), the wizard resolving the country name (open-market anchor name, else `Intl.DisplayNames`, else the fallback); tests PW-154/155/156 (`e2e/post-wizard-specs.spec.ts`), AT-67 (importer keeps tokens), TR-35 (translation keeps `{country}`), unit `catalog-tokens.test.ts`, `catalog-scope.test.ts`; `roadmap.md` "[x] Part G step 28 ({country}) screens — PW-154/155/156, AT-67, TR-35". As built the fallback key is `post.catalog.yourCountry` = "your country" / «አገርዎ» (`en.ts:2386`, `am.ts:2275`), not the decision's "the seller's country" / «የሻጩ ሀገር» wording. The `AGENTS.md` line (Part T2) has NOT landed at dev `48d3c53b` (no "MARKET-NEUTRAL WORDING" or "DEC-094" in `AGENTS.md`). DEC-097 (2026-10-01, supervisor; closed harness surface opened under G22 with a rule fixed in advance) — THE E2E ACCOUNT POOL. Supabase told the operator that organisation ethio had passed its plan's quota and that its Fair Use Policy applies from 2026-11-01. The usage pages showed 125,442 monthly active users on ethio-staging against 100,000 included, and 4 on ethio-prod; both projects sit in one organisation, so restrictions would hit production too. Cause: `e2e/helpers/users.ts` `createUser()` minted a fresh staging user for nearly every test (about 140 call sites) on every CI push, the nightly and every local run, about 4,000 a day, and a deleted user still counts for the month. Decision: (a) census every call site into (i) tests that need a brand-new identity, which keep minting, and (ii) tests that only need a signed-in account, which move to a pool; (b) the pool, staging only — fixed confirmed accounts `e2e-pool-<lane>-<NNN>@ethio-e2e.invalid`, never deleted by teardown; lanes never share accounts (one set per CI shard, one for the nightly, one for local runs); fresh random passwords each run through the admin API, kept in memory, so no new secret; a test leases one account per worker slot, reaped to a clean state before each lease; sized to the most concurrent leases per lane; (c) one line per run, "accounts signed in this run: <n> (pool <p>, fresh <f>)". Decision rule: ADOPT if three consecutive full green runs on the pool add no flake-ledger entry traceable to a shared account and each run's signed-in count is at most the pool size plus the (i) tests' count; otherwise REVERT to per-test minting. Rejected: turning the spend cap off and paying the overage (ESTIMATE about $55 a month and growing); the spend cap stays on. Census accepted with two rulings: the 11 auth-signout calls move to the pool wherever the test only needs a signed-in session; a pooled account gets the role its test asks for at lease, and tests that change a target account's status or roles mint that target fresh. As built: `leaseUser()`; lanes `s<shard>` on CI, `nightly` and `local`; seat = worker slot × 10 + the account's order within its test; accounts are created at first lease, not by global-setup, and roles are reset at the next lease, not at release (two deviations from the brief's wording, stated by the executor and now the documented design); still minting — mfa-stepup, auth-reset, auth-signin-errors, auth-callback, `@private-identity`, every admin-users target account and the "stranger" account of the category deny proof; AU-1 finds its admin's row by searching, because pooled accounts are old. Status (2026-10-04): built and on dev (`44e8eb85` after INC-376), PROVISIONAL. The first full run on the pool (36929256538) signed in 99 accounts (pool 25, fresh 74) and failed two tests in both projects (INC-377, INC-378), fixed in `b26bb0b3` (run 36931994260 green), with CI lanes then alternating by run-number parity (`s<shard>a` / `s<shard>b`). The decision rule was clarified (bring-up fixes for deterministic failures are allowed until the first fully green run) and then replaced by DEC-099 after a pool-traceable flake (INC-380): reset by census, the three-green count restarted at zero, the next pool-traceable red or flake reverts with no exception. No ADOPT statement is recorded through 2026-10-05: under DEC-099's restarted count two green runs were counted (`fb1063cb`, `34627301`), adoption was then held for a reset-timing line that was never built, and "test-account pool adoption" was named for the close-out bundle on 2026-10-03 (block S49); the pool is in use on every run (the report of run 37264070069 prints "accounts signed in this run: 5 (pool 2, fresh 3)" for the smoke source); `docs/features/e2e-harness.md` still reads "adopted provisionally 2026-10-01" at dev `48d3c53b` (line 339).

DEC-099 (2026-10-01; no operator words recorded — the supervisor put the choice to him as "Pasting it is your approval. If you prefer the revert, tell me "revert the pool" instead", and he pasted the prompt) — THE ACCOUNT POOL RESETS BY CENSUS, NOT BY A HAND-WRITTEN LIST, AND ITS ADOPTION COUNT RESTARTS AT ZERO. One declared map in a pure-data module, `e2e/helpers/pool-reset-map.ts` (no imports): every place per-account state can live — every table in `src/integrations/supabase/types.ts` with a column holding a user id (the supervisor counted 19: attribute_import_revisions, audit_log, category_country_exclusions, category_import_revisions, country_root_order, coverage_plans, entity_translations, impersonation_sessions, languages, listing_revisions, listings, location_import_revisions, profiles, screening_verdicts, translator_languages, ui_translation_revisions, ui_translations, user_directory, user_roles — plus rate_limits, keyed by the id in `key`), the auth-side state (identities, factors, sessions, metadata, a pending email or phone change) and storage objects under a user's id — is either RESET (the reaper returns it to what `handle_new_user()` leaves) or EXEMPT with a one-line reason (attribution and history columns). `reapPoolAccount()` resets everything marked RESET; as built the reaper gained `translator_languages`, open impersonation sessions, `listing_revisions` and the e-mail re-set. THE PHONE RULE, CLAUSES R1–R6 (INC-382; text of bundle 2 step 2, `attr_contact_like(text)`). A "run" is digits joined by at most two of these between digits: space, dot, hyphen, round bracket; a leading + belongs to the run. D is the run's digit count; a group is an unbroken string of digits. A text matches when: R1, a run starts with + and D is 8 or more; R2, a run's first digit is 0 and D is 9 to 15; R3, a group has 10 or more digits, or exactly 9 digits starting with 7 or 9; R4, D is 9, the first digit is 7 or 9, and every group has at least 2 digits; R5, the groups are 3-3-4, or 1-3-3-4 starting with 1; R6, the text holds an e-mail address, or a t.me/ or wa.me/ link. Nothing else matches. Must match (18): "+251 911 234 567" · "+251911234567" · "0911 23 45 67" · "0911234567" · "911234567" · "911 234 567" · "91 123 4567" · "09 11 23 45 67" · "251911234567" · "00251911234567" · "call 0911-234567" · "0911.23.45.67" · "(404) 555-1234" · "404.555.1234" · "+1 404 555 1234" · "abebe@example.com" · "t.me/abebe_shop" · "wa.me/251911234567". Must not match (16): "Sizes 42 43 44 45" · "Sizes 38 39 40 41 42 43" · "Sizes 90 92 94 96 98" · "Corolla 2008 1300cc" · "Bole Road, House 1234, 3rd floor" · "Model 320D" · "2015 2016 2017 models" · "was 150000 now 120000" · "150000000 birr" · "2023 12000 km" · "120 x 60 x 75 cm" · "Plot 25, Block 14, House 1234" · "1,500,000" · "ISBN 978-99944-0-000-0" · "Yeka, woreda 12, house 456" · "500 ETB per kg, minimum 10 kg". "The two lists are the judge": every row is an ASSERT in the migration and a case in the client mirror's unit test. Status: in force since 7423f49a. These R-numbers are a different series from the visibility plan's R1–R9 below.

DEC-104 (2026-10-02, supervisor; a harness change named as a DEC with its adoption rule fixed in advance) — THE TEST SERVICE CLIENT RETRIES A DROPPED CALL (fixes INC-385). New `e2e/helpers/net-retry.ts`, `retryingFetch(input, init)`: when fetch THROWS (no response at all) it waits and tries again, at most 3 retries after 300 ms, 1,500 ms and 5,000 ms (the waits injectable for the unit test); any Response is returned as it is, whatever its status — "A 4xx or 5xx is the server's answer and is never retried"; every method is retried, and "A replayed insert whose first copy landed must surface as the database's own duplicate error, never be swallowed"; when the retries run out it throws a TypeError naming the cause code and the attempt count; each retry appends one line to a run ledger (method, path without the query string, cause code, attempt number — never a header, a key or a body). `adminClient` (`e2e/global-setup.ts`), the only service-role client under `e2e/`, passes it as `global.fetch`; `scripts/e2e-migration-preflight.ts` also uses the service key but lies outside `e2e/` and was left as it is by ruling. `e2e/global-teardown.ts` prints "[e2e:teardown] transport retries this run: N" with counts by method and by cause code and how many ran out, even when N is 0. Unit test `src/test/e2e-net-retry.test.ts`. Rationale (stated as a hypothesis until a cause code is logged): the runtime retries a read on a closed socket by itself and does not retry a write; every one of the "fetch failed" entries in the flake ledger since 2026-09-13 is a write, and since INC-383 a failed cleanup write fails its test. Pre-committed rule (in `docs/features/e2e-harness.md`): "ADOPT after five consecutive full CI runs with no failure or flake that is a transport error in a service-client call, and with the teardown line present in every source. If any failure is traced to a replayed insert, the POST retry is removed and the rest stays." Rejected: recording the failure without a fix, which was the first disposition of the same morning and was withdrawn after the second red. Status (2026-10-05): built and landed (`5e09c8d3`); run 37038531279 was counted as the first clean run of five; no later tally and no ADOPT statement is recorded through 2026-10-05 — adoption OPEN. The teardown line is present in the newest report (run 37264070069: "transport retries this run: 0 (by method: none; by code: none; ran out: 0)" for smoke; "fetch failed" did not recur as a gating failure in the runs of 2026-10-04 → 10-05 read for this check: 37241062194, 37244952955, 37249574367, 37251884569, 37256219728, 37264070069). The executor's later local runs in this period each reported 0 transport retries.

DECISIONS OF THIS PERIOD THAT RECEIVED THEIR NUMBERS IN THE NEXT ONE. The eight decisions below were made by the operator on 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-03 and saved the same day in the project memory, with the note that they would enter the repository ledger "with the next brief Lovable receives after bundle 2, as three decisions that amend REQ-007 and REQ-008: contact visibility, alias rules, and the store page and address". The numbers DEC-106 to DEC-113 were assigned on 2026-10-03 in the supervisor's running record; the full paragraphs, with what was built, are in the next session block. What was decided here, and in what words:
- Contact visibility (later DEC-106; amends REQ-007). On 2026-10-02 at 19:51 the operator, told of INC-389, asked for research before any decision: "need to do a detailed reaserch on this firt and need to discuss first" — whether a seller who elects to show a phone or e-mail should be visible only to logged-in users, what the industry does against data miners "and what explicit reasurance we can give for each". The supervisor's research (OLX Poland shows numbers only to signed-in users since 2021; Avito substitutes forwarding numbers; Kijiji relays e-mail; a scraper for Jiji's country sites is sold online; OWASP: no single control stops harvesting) came with a per-channel proposal. His answers at 20:12: "1. Direct channels for signed-in buyers only, with no public phone option for now? yes agree"; "2. No email channel? yes". Agreed with them: phone, second phone and WhatsApp are shown to signed-in buyers who tap to show them, the Telegram handle likewise; messages on ethio.com are for signed-in buyers ("Buyers write to you here. They never see your number."); e-mail is not offered as a channel, because messages reach the seller by e-mail notification and the address is never shown; the seller's switch stays and reads "Show to signed-in buyers"; every view is recorded and one account can open only a limited number per day; a public phone option is to be revisited when verified businesses exist. Stated limits: some buyers leave at a sign-in wall; many accounts can still collect numbers slowly; the consent wording needs a legal check under Ethiopia's Personal Data Protection Proclamation 1321/2024 before launch.
- Public links and sharing (part of the later DEC-108). His question 3 answer and his clarification at 20:25 — "most users who post in instagram are not businesses, or dont want to open busness accounts so restricting may prevent them. so are we talking about same thing or something different?" — separated two things. Sharing OUT (the seller posts the ad to their own Telegram, WhatsApp, Facebook or Instagram with a link back; ACT-G1) stays for every seller. Links IN (a website, Telegram channel or social page shown on the seller's page) belong to the optional store page and may be added by any seller who opens one, person or business; a link to a personal chat, or a WhatsApp link, is a contact detail and stays behind sign-in; every link is screened when saved. At 20:33: "on Sharing out and links in - agree with your decision earlier". Not settled: how to tell a Telegram channel from a personal account when a link is entered (left to the storefront spec).
- Seller-name rules (later DEC-107; amends REQ-008). His opening at 19:51: "currently our system suggests a numbers and we should i think avoid giveing aliase like 12345", with the wish to protect "important names including category brand names, main attributes we use, or mmajor brands impersonation" and the questions whether names come from the first and last name or the business name, whether frequent replacement is allowed, and whether a changed name stays traceable. His answers: to the brand rule, "yes, but I dont want a user to use ethio anywhere even if its ethio_coffee, etc. that may be confusing for users who see it"; to how long a previous name is shown, after asking for the risks of one year against indefinitely, "i guess 1 year is ok, I was talking about aliases not the web address"; "Does the "ethio" rule also cover the business name buyers see, including the Amharic spelling? - yes"; and again at 20:45, "same aliases cant take ethio name." The rule set as agreed and saved that evening: 5 to 30 characters, Latin letters, digits and underscore, starting with a letter, at least three letters, no run of seven or more digits, no double or edge underscores (the code then allowed 3 to 30 characters, so "12345" and a phone number passed); three suggestions to tap, built from the business name or the first and last name, never from the e-mail, with at most two digits added when a name is taken, preferring names without an underscore, an Amharic name being converted to Latin letters by a fixed table (this last point was changed on 2026-10-03, next block); any name containing "ethio" is refused, including lookalike spellings and letters split by underscores — read literally this also refuses "ethiopia" and "ethiopian", and ኢትዮጵያ in a business name, which the supervisor stated twice and the operator did not change; platform words (admin, support, official, verified, moderator, staff) are refused as whole words or at the start or end of a name, not inside another word; category, attribute, place and country names are refused as a whole name and allowed inside a longer one; brands are refused on exact match against the catalogue's brand lists (640 names then) plus a seeded list of banks, telecoms, airlines and government bodies, a brand beside only a claim word is refused ("samsung_official"), a brand beside the seller's own name is allowed ("selam_samsung"), lookalikes are folded before comparing (0/o, 1/l, rn/m); e-mail provider names are protected and a country or domain ending is refused only after a protected name ("telebirr_et" refused, "abebe_et" allowed); the AI imitation check stays as a second layer and a name it cannot judge is accepted and queued for review; one change per 30 days with one free correction within 24 hours, checking a name no longer claims it, an old name stays bound to its account and is never given to another seller; the previous name is shown in public for one year, while the full name history, the forwarding of the old address and "Member since" are permanent and an admin can hide a previous name early in a safety case; the refusal message must say why and be followed by three suggestions. Of these, the operator answered in his own words the brand rule, the "ethio" rule, the business-name extension and the one-year display; the rest are the supervisor's proposals that he covered with "I agree with the above … lets save it as agreed rule" and "save the above". VISIBILITY PLAN, ACT-G1 TO ACT-G4 AND SEARCH CONSOLE (2026-10-02).
- Origin: at 07:54 the operator turned the morning's sharing discussion into a task and asked for more: "ok, lets make that as future task and document in repo and also i want you to review and comeup with any other idea that will improve our visibility, ofcourse will work on CEO of the website, in future(tell me if best to do it now and what we need to change while we are building categories search items etc. also any other way to improve our visibility." ("CEO" is SEO.) The supervisor's answer: search-engine work needs no project of its own now, but a few rules are cheap to build in and costly to retrofit. `docs/governance/visibility-plan.md` was written through the executor at `8fa761d4`: "Nothing here is built or scheduled. Every item needs its own approved spec before a build. Candidates are ideas, not decisions."
- Its §1, sharing and our own channels (operator decision): sellers share their own listing through Telegram, WhatsApp, Facebook and copy-link buttons at the end of posting and on every public listing page; ethio.com posts automatically only on accounts it owns (its own Telegram channels by category and city, fed by a bot with every approved listing, which marks or removes its post when the listing sells or is taken down); never posting into anyone else's account, channel or group, and never publishing lists of other people's groups; a shared link shows a preview card (photo, title, price, city); only listings that passed screening (REQ-021) are shareable; later, after Meta's app review, posting to a seller's own Facebook Page or Instagram business account; candidate: a seller forwards a post from their own Telegram channel to our bot and it becomes a draft listing.
- Its §2, search-engine rules R1–R9. Decided now: R1, category slugs and option values never change once public (a change needs a redirect); R2, no hand-written search text per category — titles and descriptions come from templates filled from data, and the catalogue aliases are the search synonyms; R3, the listing title is built from the seller's answers; R4, the photo step saves one share-size image per listing and uses the listing title as each picture's text alternative. For the browse-phase (U7) spec: R5, the place is in the URL (category × city pages), a listing URL carries a permanent id plus readable words, each page names one preferred address; R6, lists, listing pages and shop pages are rendered on the server with real titles, price, make and model are marked up as structured data, and a sitemap is generated; R7, only make, model and brand filter pages are indexable; R8, a sold or removed listing keeps its page for a period and shows similar listings. For launch: R9, old ethio.com addresses redirect to their new homes, the home page and `?lang=am` carry over, gambling-spam and test pages answer "gone", and the executor platform's published address names ethio.com as the preferred address.
- Its §4, seven candidates, not decided: price pages built from our own listings; bulk upload for dealers; saved-search alerts; shop pages with a printable QR code; share results shown to the seller; a Play Store listing; invite e-mails to old ethio.com users (DEC-003).
- Tracker lines, appended to `docs/tracking/action-tracker.md` under a new prefix the supervisor first checked was free: "ACT-G1 — Share buttons and link previews (visibility-plan §1). FUTURE; rides the public listing page (U7)."; "ACT-G2 — ethio.com's own Telegram channels fed by a bot (visibility-plan §1). FUTURE."; "ACT-G3 — Search-engine rules R5–R8 enter the U7 spec; R9 enters the launch gate (visibility-plan §2)."; "ACT-G4 — The listing title built from the seller's answers joins the wizard's remaining work (R3)." CLASS RULES FORGED OR RESTATED (supervisor practice from here on; none was proposed as a numbered amendment to the supervisor instructions or to the executor's Project Knowledge, and nothing was installed by the operator):
- Every multi-turn brief opens with STEP 0: save the brief unchanged under `docs/governance/briefs/`, name the path in `roadmap.md`, read it first on every turn (INC-388).
- No prompt is produced for an agent that is mid-task; finished work is verified first, then one prompt per agent with everything folded in (operator directive).
- The record is searched before the operator is asked whether something was done; when the record is silent, the step is written so that it answers itself (operator directive).
- A whole redeclaration keeps every header attribute of the live function, and the pre-apply comparison reads `provolatile`, `prosecdef` and `proconfig` beside the argument list (INC-391). A function fix never drops and re-creates unless the argument list really changes. A migration's mark is chosen at apply time (INC-390). A corrective's proofs use RAISE EXCEPTION, not ASSERT, and check that `plpgsql.check_asserts` is not off.
- A cleanup helper throws on a failed delete; a scratch root sorts at 2,000,000 or higher; no box is read while an animation runs (INC-383, INC-384).
- A pre-committed adoption rule accompanies every harness change (DEC-104); only a thrown fetch is retried, never a server's answer.
- After changing a screen, every spec that exercises it is run, not only the new tests. The end-of-bundle run is the brief's list of specs, run in parts that finish inside one turn, at 2 workers; the full-suite proof is CI on the final commit, which the supervisor reads.
- A browser test types and measures as a person would; a walk finding outranks a green test (INC-394).
- The executor runs its browser tests once per turn, at the end; red-first runs are done together, by restoring the old screen for one run or against a copy of the app from before the brief.
- Operator bandwidth: an interim executor report is brought to the supervisor only if it asks for a ruling, reports a failure, or is the final bundle report; the wording for the operator's reply is "Continue. Do not stop after one step: work through as many steps as your turn allows, and stop only when the turn is about to end."
- Walk lines use categories verified to show the behaviour being checked.
- Product research runs research → discussion → operator decision → saved in the project memory → entered in the repository ledger with the next brief; nothing goes to the executor while it is mid-task.
- Curator: removing an option goes links first, then definitions, as two confirms; the gates are 1,500 options per list (any list above 400 named in the change note) and 150 values per allowed list; an option holds at most five finder words.

DEC-106 (2026-10-02, operator "yes agree") — CONTACT DETAILS AND EXACT PINS ARE FOR SIGNED-IN BUYERS ONLY. A listing's direct contact channels (phone, second phone, WhatsApp, Telegram) and its exact map pin are private: no visitor and no other user can read them through the data API. A signed-in buyer sees them only by asking ("Show contact"), receives only the channels the seller switched on, and each first look at a listing is recorded and counted against a daily limit per account (dial `contact_reveal`, 30 per day); a second look at the same listing on the same day is not counted and the owner is never counted. The seller's switch reads "Show to signed-in buyers". There is no public phone option and no email channel for now. "Messages on ethio.com" is the default channel, always on, and cannot be switched off. An approximate pin is blurred on the server (rounded to two decimals) and the area drawn around it has a radius of 800 m, so the real spot always lies inside it. The decision amends REQ-007. Rationale: the operator asked on 2026-10-02 for research before deciding; it found that phone numbers on classifieds are harvested (a scraper for Jiji's country sites is sold online) and that peers moved to signed-in or relayed contact, and INC-389 had shown that the columns were readable by anonymous callers. Rejected: a public phone option; an email channel. Status (2026-10-04): built in bundle 3 steps 7 and 10 — M1 b9aa66a4 → mark 20261003220000 and M1b 2a467fcc → mark 20261003223000 on ethio-prod and ethio-staging; screens of Part B; tests PR-21, PW-12; on main at 9ba4ff73. Not built: the buyer-facing "Show contact" button (the door `reveal_listing_contact` is built and waits for the public ad page), and messaging itself, on which the line "We email you when a message arrives" depends.

DEC-107 (2026-10-02, operator "yes, but I dont want a user to use ethio anywhere even if its ethio_coffee"; one detail changed 2026-10-03, operator "yes") — THE SELLER-NAME RULES. The seller name (alias) is the public name of a seller and the future address of the seller's page. Shape: 5 to 30 characters of a–z, 0–9 and underscore, starting with a letter, with at least three letters, no run of seven or more digits, no underscore at either end and no two together. Every comparison is made on a fold that is never stored: lower case; underscores removed; 0→o, 1→l, 3→e, 4→a, 5→s; then rn→m; for Amharic, spaces and punctuation removed and same-sound letters equal. The rules run in this order and the first that matches refuses, each with its own message in English and Amharic: (a) shape; (b) the folded name contains "ethio" — this also refuses a business name containing "ethio" or «ኢትዮ»; (c) a role word (admin, administrator, support, official, verified, moderator, staff) or a function word (login, logout, signin, signup, verify, password, payment) as a whole part or at the start or end, so that "badminton_shop" stays allowed; (d) exact match with a site word, a category slug or English category name, the English name of any place or country, a catalogue brand name, or a protected handle; (e) a protected name beside only claim words (store, shop, official, agent, a country code and the like); (f) taken — another account holds the name now or held it before. The business name, which is what buyers see for a business, is judged by rules b, d and e (operator "yes", 2026-10-03). Checking a name does not claim it; it is claimed when the contact step is saved. Every name an account has held is kept and is never issued to another account; the first name is free; afterwards one change in 30 days, with one correction within 24 hours that does not count; for 365 days after a change the seller line shows "previously <old name>", and it always shows "Member since <month year>". Three suggestions follow every refusal, each already checked as free, built from the business name or the first and last name, never from the email or the display name, preferring forms without an underscore and adding at most two digits. An admin may assign a reserved name, with a recorded reason of at least ten characters and the audit row 'user.alias_assigned'. The AI imitation check stays as a second layer; when the AI is unavailable the name is accepted and 'alias.unchecked' is audited. Protected lists: 331 site, role and function words; the curator's 435 reserved names with 2,162 folded handles; 78 exact-only words; the catalogue's brand and make options (633 folded names in 40 lists, read live). Changed on 2026-10-03: suggestions are made only from a name typed in Latin letters; an Amharic name gets no suggestion and a hint asks for Latin letters. Rationale: impersonation of banks, telecoms, public bodies and of the site itself; the operator did not want numeric names such as "12345" or the word "ethio" in any seller's name because it would confuse buyers; the name is also the store address (DEC-108). Rejected: allowing "ethio" inside a longer name such as "ethio_coffee" (the supervisor's first proposal, overruled by the operator); transliterating Amharic names by a fixed table for suggestions (it writes ትግስት as "tigst"). On how long the previous name is shown the operator said "i guess 1 year is ok"; the record of it is kept permanently. Status (2026-10-04): built — M2 18556a32 → marks 20261004010309 and 20261004020000 on ethio-prod and ethio-staging; screens and routes of steps 18–22; tests `alias-rules.test.ts`, PW-130, PW-131, AU-12; on main at 9ba4ff73. Later changes to the contact step belong to bundle 4.

DEC-108 (2026-10-02, operator "I agree with the above but want to know if its going to affect usability, performance etc? if it doesnt lets save it as agreed rule then. same aliases cant take ethio name.") — THE STORE ADDRESS IS ethio.com/<name> AT THE ROOT. A seller's optional store page will live at ethio.com/<seller name>, replacing the July decision ethio.com/@name in REQ-008; the seller name is the address, so one name serves both. The store page is optional and open to any seller, person or business; public links (website, channel, social page) attach to it for any seller who opens one, each link screened, while a personal chat or WhatsApp link stays a contact detail behind sign-in. Safeguards, so that no site page can be mistaken for a seller: seller names have the DEC-107 shape (five characters or more, no hyphen); every first path segment of the site's own routes is shorter than five characters, or contains a hyphen, or is on the reserved site-word list; an automatic check fails the build otherwise; the site's own pages win; category and place lists stay under /c/; a daily job counts accounts whose name the rules refuse today. Rationale: the operator wanted the simplest, shortest address; "@" reads like an email address (ethio.com/@gmail.com) and /shop/ makes the address longer. Rejected: ethio.com/shop/<name>; ethio.com/@<name>. The supervisor's usability and performance review, saved at the operator's request, found no performance concern (a seller page is one indexed lookup by name; addresses that are not name-shaped are rejected by shape). Status (2026-10-04): the guard is built in bundle 3 step 23 — `scripts/site-words.txt`, `scripts/check-root-routes.ts` with its self-test in the "Build, typecheck, lint" job, and the pg_cron job 'seller-name-sweep' writing `seller_name_sweep_runs` (in M2); on main at 9ba4ff73. Not built: the store page route, public links, the verified badge and the admin path that gives a protected organisation its own business name (it comes with verified businesses).

DEC-109 (2026-10-02, operator "yes agree with all you mentioned, proceed") — THE PRICE PAGE OWNS THE DEAL. The unit of sale, the size of one unit (net weight, volume), pieces per pack and the quantity available move from the specifications page to the price page of the posting wizard, beside the price and the negotiable switch; when the offer is rent, lease or hire the price page asks the price period; the minimum term (a number with its own unit) and the payment terms are asked there too. No relationship already built between these rows and the other attributes may be lost. Rationale, in the operator's reasoning of 2026-10-02: the unit of sale, the quantity and the size of one unit are more related to the price than to the specifications, and hire and rental periods and payment terms are all related to price. It reverses the placement of 2026-09-30 (the unit asked on the specifications page, item N2), which the bundle 4 brief retires. Status at the end of this period: decided, not built, queued for bundle 4. Status (2026-10-04): built in bundle 4 Part B — M5 20261004144146_923dd4cb → mark 20261004090000 (`deal_group`, `deal_keys`, `price_basis_in_force`, `listings.price_unit`) and the price-page screens, tests PW-136 to PW-139; on main at fcc9b822, run 37241062194; walked by the operator on 2026-10-05 after the Publish of turn 10 (walk line 2: the price page's unit, Serves and the built title; line 3: a unit held by the type — "OK"; the walk's defects were elsewhere: INC-434, INC-435, INC-436). The rent and hire period rows themselves are catalogue rows owed by the curator after bundle 4 (the engine batch, not yet sent).

DEC-114 (2026-10-03, operator "agree with your recommendations. yes next step. make sure everything is secure and doesnt cause further issues.") — THE EXECUTOR RUNS ONLY THE TOUCHED SPECS LOCALLY; CI ON THE FINAL COMMIT IS THE FULL-SUITE PROOF. The executor never runs the whole E2E suite inside its turn. Its local run covers the tests for the files it changed; CI keeps running every test on every push, and nothing reaches main until CI is fully green; a new test must still fail on the old screen first, and those red runs are done together. Rationale: the operator's directive of 2026-10-03 that a single turn's test run was taking more than an hour, with his condition "I am not saying we have to do fewer tests … I dont want to make it less secure less comprehensive in terms of testing"; the delay came from the executor repeating inside its turn (about two hours) what CI does in about 22 minutes. Rejected: moving more tests to the nightly — the largest candidate, the admin console tests (about a third of all test time), would save only a few minutes per commit on six shards, and a break there could sit unnoticed for up to a day. Status (2026-10-04): in force since the bundle 3 brief; tightened by DEC-119.

DEC-115 (2026-10-03, same approval) — A SCRIPT CHOOSES THE LOCAL TESTS, UNDER A DECISION RULE FIXED IN ADVANCE. `scripts/e2e-select.ts` prints the E2E spec files a change must run: one table maps source areas to spec globs; a changed spec selects itself; a changed E2E helper selects every spec that imports it; a migration selects the areas named on its `-- e2e-areas:` header line and ALL without one; an unmapped file under `src/` or a harness file (`playwright.config.ts`, the global setup and teardown, `scripts/serve-e2e-node.ts`) selects ALL. `bun run e2e:changed` runs the list locally; a self-test in the build job fails when a spec is reachable from no area or an area's glob matches nothing. No CI test job, shard or lane changes. A decision was required because the E2E harness is a closed surface (G22). Decision rule, recorded before any result: over the next ten CI runs that follow a local selector run, count the CI failures in specs the selector did not print; 0 or 1, keep the script; 2 or more, widen the table or return to naming the specs in each brief. Rationale: the choice of local tests had been left to the executor's judgment, and on the morning of 2026-10-03 it changed the place step without running the older place-step tests. Status (2026-10-04): built in bundle 3 Part 0 (39f19b2b; `docs/features/e2e-harness.md`, "Choosing specs by what changed"). The rule is still running: no tally of the ten runs is recorded in the repository, the supervisor's notes or the transcript, and DEC-119 limited the selector's local use to lists of five files or fewer.

DEC-116 (2026-10-03, operator "I dont want cost to rise while we are still building, but wants to make it difficult to access for outside users. if the cost raises that much now … then best to hold on that until launch.") — THE REPOSITORY STAYS PUBLIC WHILE BUILDING AND GOES PRIVATE AT LAUNCH. Rationale: on a private repository GitHub Actions is billed; the supervisor's ESTIMATE was about 160 billable minutes per completed run at $0.006, about $0.96 a run, and 36 completed runs in three days, so $300–600 a month at the current pace. A second reason not to switch now: the supervisor's session reads the repository only as a public visitor — its GitHub connection is signed in to the operator's account and is not rate limited, but the repository is not attached to the session, and the session has no tool to attach it — so a switch to private would end all reading of code and CI. Consequences: a launch-gate item — attach the repository to the supervisor's session first, test, and only then switch; the CI cost plan (GitHub's runners or a runner of our own, which is a harness change needing its own decision under G22) is decided then; the data lock that costs nothing was built at once (INC-397); and, because the repository is public, detailed notes on an open security hole enter it only after the fix is live. Rejected: the supervisor's recommendation to switch to private before the bundle 3 brief was saved. Status (2026-10-05): decided; the launch-gate line is not yet in `docs/governance/launch-gate.md` (dev `48d3c53b`). On 2026-10-04 (13:54 and 14:05 local) the operator asked whether anyone copies the public repository; the standing decision was kept (block S51: public while building, private at launch, access test first; ESTIMATE of going private now 300–600 US dollars a month).

DEC-117 (2026-10-03, operator "active until should for now be indefinate and no date but user can change it to specific date and may need to have a control on admin side how long we give the publication time to be posted depending the level or type of advertizment- need to buld that") — LISTING LIFETIME: NO END DATE BY DEFAULT. An ad has no end unless the seller sets a date or its category holds a limit; the admin sets the limit by category now and by ad level (plan) later. Rationale: the operator's priority, stated on 2026-09-28, is to get many products posted, so a listing stays until the seller removes it. Known cost: ads for sold items stay up until the seller removes them; a "still available?" reminder and notices before an ad expires can cover that later. Status at the end of this period: decided, not built (with INC-400). Status (2026-10-04): built in bundle 4 step 16 — M5 923dd4cb → mark 20261004090000; test PR-23; the review step's "Stays up until you take it down." and the admin field "Listing lifetime (days)"; on main at fcc9b822; no walk line for the lifetime is recorded (the 2026-10-05 walk list had none). Lifetime by plan level waits for the posting-limits bundle ("admin posting limits and AI switches" in the operator-facing list of 2026-10-04).

DEC-118 (2026-10-03) — PHONE NUMBERS ARE READ BY libphonenumber-js/min 1.11.18, LOADED ON DEMAND. The contact step reads every typed number with `parsePhoneNumberFromString` from `libphonenumber-js/min`, pinned at exactly 1.11.18 (the version `phone-plans.ts` was taken from), loaded by a dynamic import when the contact step opens, never imported statically, and listed in FORBIDDEN in `scripts/check-marketplace-imports.mjs` so the first-paint budget cannot regress. The supervisor measured a parse-only build at 28.8 KB gzip ("about 29 KB"). It is the first dependency of its kind, so Knowledge rule A7 applied (the installed package's exports and a smoke proof were pasted). If the library cannot be loaded the step says so and offers a retry; it never falls back to another rule. Rationale: the box knew only each country's number length and a hand-written cleaning rule saved wrong numbers (INC-402); the operator asked whether the box knows each country's format. Decided by the supervisor inside the bundle 3 brief, which the operator approved by pasting it. Status (2026-10-04): built in bundle 3 Part B (`src/features/posting/phone-parse.ts`; PW-125, PW-126, PW-128); on main at 9ba4ff73.

DEC-119 (2026-10-03, operator "We need to make sure we make lovable faster as dicussed and planned earlier.") — SPEED RULES FOR THE EXECUTOR. Issued as "RULINGS 2", replacing the brief's "Local E2E" line and its end-of-bundle local run: each turn starts by reading CI for the executor's last commit, and a red is fixed before new work; local E2E per turn is only the spec files changed or added in that turn, on both projects at 2 workers, with the selector's list added only when it names five spec files or fewer; there is no end-of-bundle local run — a bundle closes on CI green for its final commit; the whole `bun run test:unit`, typecheck, lint and the whole-tree `format:check` before each commit stay; the executor does not stop between parts, only for a migration's apply line, a ruling the brief cannot answer, or the end, and a turn that ends mid-work says three lines: done, left, CI. Decision rule: a CI red in a spec the executor did not run locally that is still red after its next turn sends that area back to the selector's full list for the rest of the bundle. Refined the same night: at most three spec files per turn, and a helper swap across many specs is CI's to prove ("RULINGS 3"); the red-first rule applies to defect fixes only, and a run cancelled by a later push still lists the failures of the shards that finished, which are read as red ("RULINGS 6"). Rationale: a full CI run takes about 22 minutes and already proves the whole suite, while the executor's local runs were being cut off by its turn's time limit. Status (2026-10-04): in force; written into the bundle 4 brief's HOW TO WORK, which cites DEC-119 for the decision rule. No area was recorded as sent back under the rule.

WORDS USED IN THIS BLOCK. A "bundle" is one brief for the executor, saved under `docs/governance/briefs/`, built over several executor turns and closed by a green CI run on its final commit and an operator walk. Bundle 3 is the contact-and-seller-name bundle (security doors, contact step, seller-name rules; its migrations M1, M1b, M2 and M3 are recorded in the previous block). Bundle 4 is the posting-wizard bundle. "M4" to "M6" are the supervisor's running names for the migrations of these two bundles. A "door" is a database function the app calls. A "mark" is the row a migration writes into `public.migration_marks`; the executor ends a migration turn with the line "apply <fragment of the file name> → expect mark <value>" and the operator reads the mark back after applying. A "healer" is a follow-up migration file that only writes a missing ledger row or a later mark, because a landed migration file is never edited. "Red first" means the test is shown failing before the fix lands. A "walk" is the operator's check of the published site against a numbered list written by the supervisor. Commit and CI times are UTC; the operator's messages are dated in his local time (UTC−4).
