CLASS RULES FORGED OR RESTATED IN THIS BLOCK (in force from the day adopted; carried to the next instructions version — G46).
- The stop report of a migration that says the production apply SUCCEEDED is itself the operator's cue: he applies the new migration to staging, presses "Re-run failed jobs" and brings the report; the supervisor reads the file in parallel. He does not apply when the report says the apply failed or ends in a question. Block S56 had already written this rule (with one exception class: a migration that removes or rewrites existing rows); briefs v2 and v3 and both rulings of turn 3 nevertheless carried "wait for my go" — S121 — and D86 is the operator's own statement of the rule.
- The database tool is handed a migration's FINAL text once: never a stub, a comment or a draft; a scratch draft does not outlive the turn (INC-491 at its third occurrence; in AGENTS.md since turn 3).
- A ruling or brief step never depends on a file in the executor's scratch space surviving a turn boundary; what must survive is in the repository (S119).
- An expectation about the DATABASE in a brief (a count, a set, a shape) is taken from live rows the executor pasted, not from a static reading of the migration files; where only a static reading exists the brief says so and tells the executor to shape the statement from the rows it reads (S118).
- A function that judges an answer reads that answer through ONE normalisation at its entry; a second reader of the raw input is a defect (INC-490 — "one function, two readings of the same input").
- Every bundle-close CI read includes the conclusion line of `nightly-status.md` (the nightly of 2026-10-07 was written at 09:39Z, was not looked at in the CI read of 09:58Z, and was read at 10:40Z).
- A platform package bump is read by comparing the two public tarballs before it is ruled (DEC-156); a change that only the platform's own build environment makes is judged on the published site, not by CI (DEC-158).
- A rule restated to an agent carries the term that decides its edge cases, quoted from the code that enforces it (S120; S82's family).
- A census that must read every file line by line is its own executor turn, or is the supervisor's own reading; it is not added to a turn that also changes code (S122). A proof asked of the executor must be able to FAIL on the day it is run (S122: F1.5 could not, once the re-run had reset the row).
- The close of a bundle that changes an existing string carries "Sync keys", the Amharic import and "Approve all reviewed" as numbered operator steps (INC-488).
- A setting the operator holds is read on his screen before it is described to him as on or off (restated from S56; the leaked-password switch).

THE FEED ENGINE (D99–D101; bundle 10; spec `docs/governance/feed-engine-spec.md`, imported by this records turn with its approval line). Today the feed reads every active listing with no order and no page and sorts in the browser (INC-505), a category's page reads only its own category (INC-503), a subcategory's address selects nothing (INC-504), and the place filter is not built. The approved design: one table `feed_index` with a row for every active listing under each of its category's ancestors and each of its place's ancestors (its coverage places included), ordered by tier, then newest, then id; written inside the write doors at publish, edit, expiry and every state change, re-built for a category move by a job with a heartbeat, checked against the listings every night; one function `feed_page` and one route `/api/feed` that read a page of 20 after a cursor (keyset paging, never an offset), with the catalogue's cache headers for visitors who are not signed in; the widening ladder city → region → country → world when a step has fewer than 8 listings. THE FIVE DECISIONS (D101): (1) the targets, frozen before building — at 100,000 scratch listings on staging every page shape answers in 50 ms or less at the 95th percentile, a page weighs 30 KB or less, a cached page's first byte comes within 100 ms, and the first page shows within 1.5 s after the shell on a slow 3G profile (indicative); (2) "nearer step first, newest within a step" orders the feed instead of an exact distance sort — REQ-005's order for the feed is AMENDED by this decision; (3) the widening threshold is 8; (4) 20 per page, the next page loaded as the last card comes into view; (5) the engine is built next, before bundle 9's second half. Three turns (ESTIMATE, the spec's §7): E1 `feed_index`, its refresh function, the backfill of today's active listings and the consistency check (Tier A, one migration); E2 the write doors call the refresh, the tree-change re-index job, `feed_page` and `/api/feed` with its cache (Tier A, a second migration and a new public read); E3 the feed on the route with cursor paging, subcategory addresses resolved through the whole tree, the breadcrumbs and the performance job (Tier B).

WHAT THE FIX TURNS BUILT.
- `CutText` (src/components/ui/cut-text.tsx) is one inline grid cell holding three elements:
  - the visible element holds the whole name, so the accessible name and textContent are the name, once;
  - an unpainted, `aria-hidden` element whose CSS-generated content (`.cut-floor::before`, the first five graphemes and "…") sets the smallest width;
  - an unpainted, `aria-hidden` element whose generated content (`.cut-full::before`, the whole name, breakable anywhere) sets the widest width.
  So a name never shows fewer than its first five characters, a name of five or fewer stays whole, and a row of cut names can shrink.
- `useLabelRoom` (src/components/ui/use-label-room.ts): when a row overflows, its optional parts step aside in order — the label first (`sr-only`, still read by screen readers), then the elements its caller names (the place boxes' arrows, `hidden`).
- The input marker (src/lib/input-modality.ts, installed once in RootComponent's effect) sets `html[data-input]` to pointer or keyboard. One CSS rule empties the ring variables on buttons, links and menu roles after pointer input. Text inputs keep their ring. Focus still returns to the control.
- Twenty user-facing cut names moved to CutText:

WHAT BUNDLE 10 BUILT (the feed-engine spec of D99–D101, docs/features/feed-engine.md).
- E1 — the index. `feed_index` holds one row per listing per category key (its own and every ancestor's, through the pointers) per place key (its place, every parent, and the everywhere key, the nil uuid), keyed (category, place, tier rank, published time, id) and read backwards; a second index on listing_id. `feed_index_refresh(listing)` takes the listing's row lock and rewrites its rows; active listings without a publish time get none. The backfill and its consistency check ran inside the migration under SHARE locks. Browsers cannot read the table or call its functions (FE-5).
- E2a — the index keeps itself right. Statement-level triggers on listings and listing_locations refresh each touched listing once per statement, inside the writer's transaction, so every write door, the expiry sweep and any future writer are covered without redeclaring a door. Tree changes (pointers; a place's parent) queue the active listings of the moved subtree in `feed_reindex_queue`; `feed_reindex_wake()` schedules the drain (`feed-reindex-drain`, every minute) only while the queue holds listings, and the drain unschedules itself when empty (version 4, the platform's rule — below). `feed_index_check_sweep()` runs daily at 03:53 UTC and writes its counts; the drain writes a heartbeat row (14 days kept), the check its row (60 days). The tier ranks premium 2 · featured 1 · regular 0 (`feed_tier_rank`, D108).
- E2b — the read door. `feed_page(category, place, after, size 1–50, default 20)`, definer and STABLE, granted to anon, authenticated and service_role — the one new public surface, named in scripts/public-surface-allowlist.txt and (from turn 12) scripts/security-lints-baseline.json. The ladder: the chosen place, each parent, then everywhere; the widest step read is the first that holds at least 8 listings of the category, else everywhere. Each step is one backward range of the key, without the listings of the step before; inside a step premium, then featured, then regular, newest first (D108). `/api/feed` answers it with a base64url cursor and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300`. FR-1–FR-8.
- E3a — Admin › Screening (D109). The ads waiting in `screening`, oldest first, 25 a page with a title search; Approve and Reject ask for confirmation, then step-up, then call `transition_listing` as the reviewer; the section opens on `listings:review` (DEC-163); the outcome in an inline live region. "Preview as buyer" opens the posting form's buyer preview. SC-1–SC-5 (SC-4 on a scratch role holding listings:review only); SC-6 (turn 14) the preview's category picture.
- E3b — the listings pages. The home and every category page read /api/feed a page at a time (20; the next page when the last card comes into view); a category's page holds its whole branch; a subcategory's address resolves through the whole tree; the page heading names the place; a step's cards sit under its label ("Listings near <place>", "All listings") and a note "Nothing here yet in your area" leads when the chosen place has none; an unknown address shows not found and asks the feed nothing; a failed read shows a Retry. The card stops printing a views count (DEC-165). Breadcrumbs follow a category's path. FS-1–FS-7, FP-1–FP-7.
- E3c — the speed judge (DEC-166, weekly from DEC-167). `feed_bench(category, place, after, runs 1–200)` (invoker, service role only) times `feed_page` inside the database; scripts/feed-bench.ts seeds 100,500 scratch active listings on ethio-staging, times six shapes (33 calls, 3 warm-ups dropped, nearest-rank p95 of 30), removes everything in a finally and writes docs/tracking/feed-bench-status.md to ci-evidence; `--clean` removes leftovers; batches of 250 with a retry on a statement timeout (INC-524). .github/workflows/feed-bench.yml (Sunday 05:10 UTC and on demand). FB-1–FB-6.
- The staging gate (DEC-168, turn 14). scripts/staging-gate.ts: the bench waits for a quiet ethio-staging before it writes (up to 40 minutes, else SKIPPED) and yields when CI, the nightly or Guard Proof starts (YIELDED, after its cleanup); the nightly waits up to 60 minutes before its tests, then runs anyway, and writes a notice for every other staging run that overlapped it; CI never waits. SG-1–SG-4.

DEC-168 (2026-10-09; supervisor under G17/G22 — infrastructure, no cost, reversible; overridable; answering the operator's "what prevents it from colliding with CI … do we have a mechanism?") — THE STAGING GATE. CI has priority; the others wait or yield. Four workflows use ethio-staging — CI, Nightly E2E, Guard Proof and Feed bench — and their concurrency groups only kept two runs of the same workflow apart.
1. Feed bench: before it writes anything, it waits until no CI, Nightly E2E or Guard Proof run is queued or running (read through the Actions API with the workflow's own token, actions: read), up to 40 minutes; still busy, or the gate unreadable → Verdict SKIPPED, with the runs named (red). While it seeds and measures it asks again at most every 15 seconds; when such a run has started it stops, cleans up and writes Verdict YIELDED (red).
2. Nightly E2E: the same wait before its tests (up to 60 minutes; still busy → it runs anyway, with a warning); after the serial full run it writes a notice for every other staging run that overlapped it, so a nightly red is read with that in hand (INC-487's need).
3. CI: unchanged — it never waits, so the executor's turns are not slowed.
Residual, stated: a CI run that starts during the bench's final cleanup (about a minute) still overlaps it. Pre-committed rule: over the next four weekly benches and fourteen nightlies, more than two SKIPPED benches or more than two nightlies that started more than 30 minutes late → the schedules move (not the gate). DECISIONS (his words are in the imported record).
- DEC-170 (supervisor under D118, listed to the operator as overridable; 2026-10-10) — on every table built on the agreed blocks the row carries Edit, Delete (red; off while the door would refuse it) and the three-dots menu with the editor's other verbs; the editor keeps its verb bar. A dialog opened from the row closes back to the table; one opened from the editor closes back to the editor (INC-150 kept).
- DEC-171 (supervisor under the operator's request "anyway to reduce this?", 2026-10-11 05:26 local; the rule frozen before the numbers) — eight E2E shards; the preflight waits up to 25 minutes for a staging apply; the nightly 06:00 → 18:00 UTC; the feed bench Sunday 05:10 → 16:10 UTC. Measured: 40 green runs, median ~26 min on 10-08 → 31–33 min on 10-11. REVERT RULE: over the next five green runs on dev, median > 29 min or two staging-load reds → six shards; median ≤ 26 min keeps eight. Its count was overridden by DEC-172 (below) after one run of 34.3 min — the supervisor's expectation of about 26–28 min was wrong (G5, recorded).
- DEC-172 (supervisor under G17 and the operator's request; the count restart overrides DEC-171's frozen count and was listed for his paste as approval; 2026-10-11) — `PWTEST_SHARD_WEIGHTS` on the shard step (read by Playwright 1.58.1; undocumented — a version that drops it falls back to equal slices), first `160:202:145:236:160:185:145:232`, re-tuned under its own rule to `148:174:195:235:148:157:195:231`. RULE frozen: five green runs after landing — median wall ≤ 30 min keeps eight weighted shards; > 30 min or two staging-load reds → weights off, six shards. Re-tune when a green run's slowest shard is ≥ 4 min longer than its quickest (docs/features/ci-guards.md).
- DEC-173 (supervisor, G17; listed for the operator's paste as approval; amends the approved Listings console spec's content-rules line; 2026-10-11) — an admin's edit is judged through step 5 of the seller's judge, with `NULL, NULL` for the end date and the places: the category postable, the specifications, the price, the title and the description; the contact step (7) and step 8 are not reached; the video link stays as sent (the table's own check matches the judge's shape). - DEC-174 (supervisor, G17; approved by the operator's paste of bundle-11-turn-34.md; 2026-10-12) — an e2e test, or a `beforeAll`, leases at most two pooled accounts; scripts/e2e-leases.ts (EL-1..EL-4) counts each test's leases through every helper and file-local function and the `beforeEach` hooks around it, and refuses a lease in a loop. CLASS RULES AND STANDING PRACTICE FROM THIS PERIOD.
- A client filter's column is checked against the role's column grant before a brief names it, and a filter test asserts a result the unfiltered list cannot give (INC-537, INC-538, S155).
- A row's three-dots menu is not modal and leaves at once when it closes; a dialog opened from the row closes back to the table (INC-539, INC-541, DEC-170).
- A table's actions column is sized for the icons its rows carry (`actionsWidth`), read box by box against its cell at 768/1024/1280 (INC-542, S158).
- No drop-down inside a toolbar panel; on a phone a panel is a modal sheet (INC-543).
- A server-paged read is drawn with its pager (INC-546); every admin table's page size is kept (`useKeptPage`; C1's T6).
- A scratch role signed into /admin holds `admin_panel:access` besides the section's permission (INC-550); a test that takes "another market" takes a real one (`openMarketCodes({ realOnly: true })`, INC-551).
- A door acting for an admin on a seller's listing judges only what the admin can change (INC-552, DEC-173).
- A detail route teaches the breadcrumb its section and its last crumb; a group without a page is plain text (INC-554, INC-557).
- An admin control that sends values computed from a read, or a form seeded from one, waits while that read re-reads or a write keyed to it is in flight (INC-558; `useSettling`, `useFollowingDraft`).
- An absence check on serialized text uses a probe that cannot occur by chance, or checks the structure (INC-559); no role-based locator while a modal is open (INC-560).
- The public category menu's rows are read through e2e/helpers/category-menu.ts only; scripts/e2e-menu-readers.ts refuses a reader built by hand (INC-561's class at its third occurrence, C3).
- An e2e test leases at most two pooled accounts (DEC-174; INC-555's class at its third occurrence).
- A test sets request headers on its own page's context; a second context only for a second person or an isolated browser state (INC-569).
- A read-everything loop pages by key, never by position (INC-568, INC-452's class); `readAllPages` is the one helper.
- A guard runs in CI or in the unit tests, proven on its planted file first; a guard no job runs is a finding (INC-563).
- A test id is assigned once; a title wrapped onto the line after `test(` is read too (INC-536; TI-5).
- The agreed tables' rules T1–T9 are written in display-primitives.md and checked by scripts/admin-tables.ts with no baseline (C1, C4); a destructive act is red on every control that performs or confirms it, checked by scripts/destructive-red.ts (C2).
- Each turn is built on a stand-in of the landing before it, and the real landing is verified equal to the stand-in byte for byte (the standing directive of 2026-10-12).
- No brief stops on the CI read: step 1 pastes what it shows and goes on; the CI read is the supervisor's (S176, S177 — the raw address is served up to 300 s stale).
- An action's outcome is drawn beside the control that produced it and comes into view when it appears (INC-570); a test of an outcome asserts it on screen, not only visible.

- THE LAWYER'S POINT (listed for counsel, not resolved; the supervisor is not a lawyer): Ethiopia's Electronic Transaction Proclamation 1205/2020 — Art. 41(2): platform operators have sellers submit their true identity, address, contacts and administrative licences and "verify and register the same"; Art. 25: a host's exemption for stored information needs that it did not know, removes on notice expeditiously, and has designated an agent for notices. Terms v1 §12 says ethio.com verifies no one; whether a free classifieds site is a "platform operator" in that sense is counsel's question at the Ethiopia-entity milestone (the standing ruling: not a launch blocker). The legal record had not cited 1205/2020 before.

DECISIONS
- D225 (the operator, 2026-10-19 02:20–02:25 local, AskUserQuestion; amends the L1 v2 spec of 2026-10-04) — the legal model: each version named by staff (a label); a change log per version, staff-only and final once published; no public "what changed" note (the supervisor's recommendation overridden); past versions not listed publicly, pending the research ("legally are we required to keep versions … if we are not legally required to disclose previous in any jurisidiction, then we email updated, and when they login after a change they have to resign … if we are required, then we may have to keep list public"); the curator researches peers' terms and privacy policies and the supervisor audits; the machinery built now, version 1 published only after the wording is approved; and (02:25) "whatever document they signup should remain with also a history of emailed documents as well inside user profile" — each person keeps every version he accepted and the legal e-mails sent to him, readable by him and by staff (legal_notices, my_legal_history, my_legal_version, record_legal_notice, admin_user_legal_history). Built in turns 1–3.
- DEC-204 (the operator, 04:2x local, AskUserQuestion — the four recommendations; (e) at 05:0x) — (a) no seller identity checks at launch, the Terms say so plainly, revisited with the lawyer at the Ethiopia-entity milestone — with his addition (04:56) that verification may be required at any time where a country's law requires it, to protect users or to look into a report (the redline's Terms §2 "Verification"; Privacy §3 and §4); (b) data stored in the United States with a SEPARATE consent tick at acceptance, servers in Ethiopia at the Ethiopia-entity milestone ("Ethiopia first"); (c) the courts of Georgia, consumers keeping their home courts and law where those apply, no arbitration, no class-action waiver; (d) the ad licence sublicensable to providers and to the services we repost to, ending on erasure except copies already shared; (e) "can not signin without accepting terms of service and privacy policy- hard stop" — the acceptance screen has no "Not now": Agree and continue, or Sign out; the public pages and /auth stay reachable. The operator's entity: Ethio.com LLC (the redline's {{operator_name}}). Built: (b) and (e) in turn 3; (a), (c) and (d) are text in the redline. DEC-130 REAFFIRMED (05:2x local, "12 months (DEC-130 as is)").
- DEC-205 (the operator, 09:4x local, "Once per ad (Recommended)"; amends DEC-129's tick on every publish, edit and renew) — the publishing statement is ticked once per ad: asked only while the ad holds no certification of exactly the statement versions in force for it (its first publish; again only for a new version or a country with its own statement); edits, renewals and photos otherwise ask nothing and record nothing; the Terms and Privacy acceptance at sign-in is unchanged.
